scope: Proposition 3.8 (Dependence of the prime threshold) of the manuscript “A power saving for intersective polynomial differences with an exponent depending only on the degree” (preprints/A-power-saving-for-intersective-polynomial-differences-with-an-exponent-depending-only-on-the-degree-October-5-2026/power-saving-intersective-polynomial-differences.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 182 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d69e417ac953581d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the auxiliary family and local choices above, the threshold P can be chosen as a function of k, P1, L, t alone so that Proposition 3.5, Lemmas 3.6 and 3.7, and (3.7) hold uniformly in l. For general fixed data, P1 may depend on h, and L may depend on h and its chosen roots. If h satisfies Condition (U) and the degree-dependent choices of P1, Ep, and L from Section 2 are used, then P and M0 depend only on k.
